data.narrative:
Star Catcher, a Series A–stage space and aerospace company founded by Andrew Rush, Michael Snyder, and Bryan Lyandvert, has raised $88M to date. The valuation universe comprises five public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and eight private peers including SpaceX, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs, though a tightly filtered peer set at identical stage and valuation tier proved insufficient for reliable median analysis.

Given data constraints, only the stage-progression method proved applicable. Using total capital raised ($88M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.0x step-up multiplier between Series A and later stages yields an implied valuation of $176M. Public Space & Aerospace comparables trade at a median EV/Sales multiple of 23.9x across six tickers, but without disclosed revenue for Star Catcher, this anchor cannot be quantified. The peer-median approach was inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage datapoints within the narrowed peer cohort.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $150M to $202M, centered on $176M. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue-based public comp anchoring, limited availability of same-stage private comparable transactions, and reliance on stage-progression mechanics as a sole quantitative method. A fuller picture would require either target revenue disclosure or disclosure of recent transactions among the identified private peer set.
